title: Will Uber's takeover of Delivery Hero be approved by BaFin before September 2026?
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if, Germany's Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) approves Uber's Offer Document for its takeover of Delivery Hero SE and the document is formally published in accordance with the WpÜG before September 1, 2026.
background:
On July 16, 2026, Uber Technologies and Delivery Hero SE entered into a [Business Combination Agreement](https://investor.uber.com/news-events/news/press-release-details/2026/Uber-Announces-Acquisition-Offer-for-Delivery-Hero/default.aspx) under which Uber will make a voluntary public takeover offer for Delivery Hero SE shareholders at €41.50 per share in cash, implying an equity value of $14.8 billion. Delivery Hero confirmed the terms in its own [newsroom statement](https://www.deliveryhero.com/newsroom/delivery-hero-and-uber-to-join-forces-to-deliver-more-for-customers-vendors-and-riders/), and Uber described the agreement in a [Form 8-K filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000155278126000382/e26302_uber-8k.htm) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

This is one of the largest acquisitions in the food delivery sector, combining Uber Eats with Delivery Hero's operations across Europe, Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East. While full completion of the acquisition is expected in the second half of 2027 due to extensive multi-jurisdictional antitrust reviews, the immediate regulatory step is securing approval in Germany.

As part of the same transaction, Delivery Hero separately agreed to sell its operations in 14 overlapping markets to SSW Partners, a New York-based investment firm, for approximately €1.4 billion. The divestment is intended to address antitrust overlap between Uber Eats and Delivery Hero in those markets and help smooth the path for regulatory approvals.

Under German takeover law (the Wertpapiererwerbs- und Übernahmegesetz, or [WpÜG](https://www.bafin.de/EN/Aufsicht/BoersenMaerkte/Unternehmensuebernahmen/unternehmensuebernahmen_node_en.html)), a bidder must prepare a formal Offer Document and submit it to Germany's Federal Financial Supervisory Authority ([BaFin](https://www.bafin.de/EN/Homepage/homepage_node.html)) for review before the document can be published. Publication of the Offer Document is the event that formally starts the acceptance period, during which Delivery Hero shareholders can tender their shares into the offer.

Once BaFin approves the Offer Document, [§14(2) WpÜG](https://www.bafin.de/SharedDocs/Standardartikel/DE/bieterpflichten_wpueg.html) requires the bidder to put it online "unverzüglich" without undue delay. The bidder also has to publish the full document in the electronic Bundesanzeiger, or make it freely available in Germany and announce where via the Bundesanzeiger, so shareholders can always get hold of it.

According to the companies' joint announcement, Uber will publish its Offer Document "following approval by BaFin," with publication and related materials to appear on the deal's official website, [delivering-value.com](https://www.delivering-value.com).

comments.author: hr185882
comments.text: The reference class for this prediction includes recent high-profile mergers and acquisitions in the tech and delivery sectors that have undergone regulatory scrutiny. Rationale reflects uncertainty given increasing scrutiny of large tech mergers.

comments.author: DaiLothbrook
comments.text: I start at 65%, reflecting a friendly transaction and the statutory schedule following the July 16 business-combination agreement. I move slightly down to 62%. Uber must submit the offer document within four weeks, after which BaFin normally has 10 working days, extendable to 15.

comments.author: Russell-viper
comments.text: Both companies' official statements are phrased in future tense as of the July 16 announcement -- the initial offer document had not yet been submitted. The 4-week statutory deadline to submit ends August 13.
